name: Multi-AZ Production
description: A pattern for deploying production workloads across multiple availability zones within a single cloud region to achieve high availability. Provides resilience against individual data centre failures while maintaining low-latency communication between components.
whenToUse: Production services requiring 99.9% or higher availability SLA
Citizen-facing services where downtime directly impacts public trust
Workloads where single-AZ failure must not cause service interruption
Services with regulatory or policy requirements for infrastructure redundancy
Applications where the cost of downtime exceeds the cost of multi-AZ deployment
whenNotToUse: Development and testing environments where single-AZ is sufficient
Internal tools with low availability requirements and acceptable maintenance windows
Workloads where multi-region DR is required (use multi-region-dr pattern instead)
Cost-constrained projects where 99% availability is acceptable
Batch processing workloads that can tolerate interruption and restart

typicalComponents.name: Multi-AZ Compute
typicalComponents.purpose: Run application instances across multiple availability zones
typicalComponents.technology: Auto Scaling Groups, VM Scale Sets, or Managed Instance Groups

typicalComponents.name: Cross-AZ Load Balancer
typicalComponents.purpose: Distribute traffic across instances in multiple AZs with health checks
typicalComponents.technology: ALB, Azure Load Balancer, or Cloud Load Balancing

typicalComponents.name: Multi-AZ Database
typicalComponents.purpose: Replicate data synchronously across AZs for zero data loss on failover
typicalComponents.technology: RDS Multi-AZ, Azure SQL HA, or Cloud SQL HA

typicalComponents.name: Cross-AZ Storage
typicalComponents.purpose: Store data with automatic replication across availability zones
typicalComponents.technology: S3, Azure Blob (ZRS), or Cloud Storage (multi-regional)

typicalComponents.name: Health Monitoring
typicalComponents.purpose: Detect AZ-level failures and trigger automatic failover
typicalComponents.technology: CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, or Cloud Monitoring

securityControls: Implement consistent security group rules across all availability zones
Ensure encryption keys are available in all AZs used by the deployment
Implement network segmentation consistently across AZs
Ensure IAM policies and service accounts work across AZ boundaries
Implement consistent logging and audit trails across all AZs
Test security controls during failover scenarios
resilienceConsiderations: Synchronous replication between AZs ensures zero data loss during failover
Automatic failover for managed services (RDS, load balancers) requires no manual intervention
Design applications to be stateless or use distributed session stores
Test failover regularly by simulating AZ failures in non-production
Ensure sufficient capacity in remaining AZs to handle full load during failure
Consider the blast radius — some failures may affect multiple AZs simultaneously
costConsiderations: Multi-AZ deployment approximately doubles compute and database costs
Cross-AZ data transfer charges apply for inter-AZ communication
Managed multi-AZ services (RDS Multi-AZ) include replication in pricing
Right-size for N+1 capacity — each AZ must handle increased load during failure
Consider the cost of downtime versus the cost of redundancy
Reserved capacity across multiple AZs for cost optimisation
operationalConsiderations: Deployment procedures must update all AZs consistently (rolling or blue-green)
Monitoring must detect AZ-level degradation before complete failure
Runbooks needed for AZ failover scenarios and recovery procedures
Capacity planning must account for running on reduced AZs during failure
Regular failover testing to validate recovery procedures work correctly
Configuration management must ensure consistency across all AZs

services.name: Application Load Balancer
services.purpose: Cross-AZ traffic distribution with health checks

services.name: Availability Zones
services.purpose: Deploy VMs and services across physically separate zones

services.name: Regional Managed Instance Groups
services.purpose: Distribute VMs across zones in a region

questionsToAsk: What is the target availability SLA and what does downtime cost the organisation?
How many availability zones should be used (2 or 3)?
What is the acceptable recovery time if an AZ fails?
Are there data consistency requirements during failover?
How will failover be tested and how frequently?
Is the application designed to be stateless or does it require session affinity?
commonMistakes: Deploying multi-AZ but not testing failover, discovering issues only during real incidents
Not provisioning sufficient capacity in remaining AZs to handle full load during failure
Using single-AZ components (e.g., single NAT gateway) that become single points of failure
Not accounting for cross-AZ data transfer costs in budget planning
Assuming multi-AZ protects against regional failures — it does not
